[[70 BBY]] and c. [[61 BBY]]''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' places [[Din Djarin]]'s first meeting with "the Client" in [[9 ABY]]. In ''[[The Mandalorian Junior Novel|Star Wars: The Mandalorian Junior Novel]]''{{'s}} adaptation of the event, the Client is described as being in his seventies, meaning that he was between seventy and seventy-nine in 9 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|ABY]]. Therefore, he must have therefore been [[Reproduction|born]] between around [[70 BBY]] and around [[61 BBY]]. |death=[[9 ABY]], [[Nevarro]]''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' |species=[[Human]]''[[Star Wars: Character Encyclopedia, Updated and Expanded Edition]]'' |gender=[[Gender|Male]][[The Mandalorian Junior Novel|''The Mandalorian'' Junior Novel]] |pronouns=He/him |height=1.83 [[meter]]s {{C|6[[Foot|ft]]}} |mass= |hair=[[Color|Gray]] |feathers= |eyes=Light blue |skin=Light |cyber= |families= |parents= |partners= |siblings= |children= |affiliation=*[[Galactic Empire]][[Star Wars: The Mandalorian: Guide to Season One|''Star Wars: The Mandalorian'': Guide to Season One]] **[[Imperial Officer Corps]] *[[Gideon's Imperial remnant]] **[[The Client's squad]]{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 7: The Reckoning}} |masters= |apprentices= }} {{Quote|It is good to restore the natural order of things after a period of such disarray, don't you agree?|"The Client," to Din Djarin|{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 1: The Mandalorian}}}} "'''The Client'''" was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] who served as an [[Imperial officer]] in the [[Galactic Empire]]. After the Empire's [[Battle of Jakku|fall]], he continued with an [[Gideon's Imperial remnant|Imperial remnant]] led by [[Moff]] [[Gideon]]. In [[9 ABY]], he and the Imperial [[scientist]] [[Doctor]] [[Penn Pershing]] operated out of a [[Imperial Remnant safe house|safe house]] on the [[planet]] [[Nevarro]], under orders to acquire and extract [[blood]] from the [[Force-sensitive]] [[Youngling|infant]] [[Yoda's species|alien]] [[Din Grogu|Grogu]]. While the infant was known as "the Child," the Client called him the "the asset." He hired many [[bounty hunter]]s from the local [[Bounty Hunters' Guild]] in [[Hunt for Grogu|pursuit]] of his goal. One such [[bounty]] [[Hunting|hunter]] was the [[Mandalorian]] [[Din Djarin]], whom the Client met at his safe house. The Imperial gave to the Mandalorian a [[beskar]] ingot as a down payment for the job and provided information and a [[tracking fob]] to secure "the asset." Djarin was successful in his [[Mission to Arvala-7|hunt]] and brought Grogu back to the safe house. Pleased with the mission's success, the Client compensated the bounty hunter with a [[camtono]] of twenty beskar ingots. When Djarin questioned what would be done to the infant, the Imperial shut down his inquiries and compelled him to leave. The Client and Pershing extracted blood from Grogu, with the doctor keeping the infant from dying despite his colleague's lack of care for "the asset"'s life. Meanwhile, Djarin, having a change of heart, returned and [[Incident on Nevarro|rescued]] the Child from the safe house. As a result, the Client took control of [[Nevarro City]] with Imperial reinforcements and sent bounty hunters from the Bounty Hunters' Guild to retrieve Grogu. The Guild agent [[Greef Karga]] coaxed Djarin back to Nevarro to seize the Child back for the Client but shifted loyalties and instead chose to help the Mandalorian and his allies. Djarin was [[Stuncuffs|cuffed]] and taken by Karga and the Mandalorian's ally [[Carasynthia Dune|Cara Dune]] to the Client in the [[Nevarro school|Nevarro Common House]], bringing along an empty [[Hover pram|pram]] as a decoy in Grogu's place. There the Imperial spoke with Djarin about the planet [[Mandalore]]'s rebelliousness against the late Empire and then requested to see the Child. Before he could do so, the Client was interrupted by a call from Gideon. The moff asked his associate to check the pram again for the infant before instructing his [[Gideon's guard|squad]] of [[death trooper]]s to [[Clash on Nevarro|fire]] on the [[Cantina|common house]] and [[Death|kill]] the Client and his men. ==Biography== ===The job=== {{Quote|There is one job.''"
"''Let's see the puck.''"
"''No puck. Face to face. Direct commission. Deep pocket.''"
"''Underworld?''"
"''All I know is no chain code. Do you want the chit or not?|Greef Karga gives Din Djarin information on a new bounty|audio=DjarinKarga-Bounty-TMS1C1.flac|}} [[Reproduction|Born]] between around [[70 BBY]] and around [[61 BBY]], the [[human]] [[Gender|male]] known as "the Client" became an [[Imperial officer]] in the [[Galactic Empire]], earning for himself an Imperial [[medal]]lion indicative of high honor. The Empire fell at the [[Battle of Jakku]] in [[5 ABY]], but the Client continued to serve with remnants of the [[Politics|government]] and wore his medal in doing so, eventually coming to work with an [[Gideon's Imperial remnant|Imperial remnant]] led by the [[warlord]] [[Moff]] [[Gideon]]. While under Gideon's [[Commanding officer|command]], the Client resided in{{EncyclopediaCite|Lando Calrissian and Other Characters From the Galaxy}} a [[Imperial Remnant safe house|safe house]] in [[Nevarro City]] on the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[planet]] [[Nevarro]],''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian Handbook]]'' keeping a low profile there{{Topps|set=2020 Topps Star Wars Holocron Series|cardname=The Client|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/231065/cid/15795190/2020-Topps-Star-Wars-Holocron-Series-Emp-17-The-Client}} by having only a small group of [[stormtrooper]]s for protection. [[Doctor]] [[Penn Pershing]],{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 19: The Convert}} a [[scientist]] who had also served as an [[officer]] within the Empire, worked under the Client and Gideon and had a [[laboratory]] in the safe house. [[File:Grogu-TheMandalorian.png|thumb|right|300px|"The Client" was tasked with retrieving Grogu (pictured).]] In [[9 ABY]], the Client was under orders from Gideon to acquire and extract [[blood]]{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 12: The Siege}} from [[Din Grogu|Grogu]], a [[Force-sensitive]] male [[Youngling|infant]] of the same [[Yoda's species|species]] as former [[Jedi]] [[Grand Master]] [[Yoda]].{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 13: The Jedi}} At the [[time]], the infant was known only as "the Child," though the Imperial referred to him as "the asset." The Imperials possessed the coordinates of the Child's last known location and [[tracking fob]]s that could follow "the asset"'s position when close enough. Needing his task to be done quickly and quietly, the Client set up{{SWCT|set=2021 Base|cardname=The Client}} a high paying{{InsiderCite|216|The Journey of Din Djarin}} but off-the record job in order to use [[bounty hunter]]s to [[Hunt for Grogu|retrieve]] Grogu, and informed [[Greef Karga]], the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild]]'s agent on Nevarro, of the job. Rather than providing the traditional [[Holopuck|puck]] and [[chain code]], the Client wished to meet the [[Hunting|hunters]] who accepted the job face to face, unwilling to give them any more information than Grogu's age and tracking signature,{{Topps|set=2020 Topps Star Wars: The Mandalorian Season 1|cardname=The Client|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/233698/cid/15449358/2020-Topps-Star-Wars:-The-Mandalorian-Season-1-5-The-Client}} and provided [[chit]]s for them to visit his safe house. Many [[bounty]] hunters from the Guild took up the job, though none were successful. During this time, Karga informed the [[Mandalorian]] bounty hunter [[Din Djarin]] of the offer after he turned in his previous bounties. After the Mandalorian chose to take the job, the guild agent notified the Client that Djarin was coming to meet him, describing the hunter as the best in the [[parsec]] but also expensive. ===The meeting=== {{Quote|Greef Karga said you were coming.''"
"''What else did he say?''"
"''He said you were the best in the parsec. ''[…]'' He also said you were expensive. Very expensive.|audio=Client-Expensive.flac|"The Client" and Din Djarin|}} [[File:The_Client_standoff.png|thumb|left|300px|"The Client" defused a standoff between his stormtroopers and Din Djarin.]] The Client waited at his desk in the safe house, guarded by four armed stormtroopers as he anticipated Djarin's arrival.{{EncyclopediaCite|Post-Galactic Civil War and the Mandalorian}} A [[GNK-series power droid]] led Djarin to the room, where the Client greeted him. Pershing then hastily entered the room, startling the Mandalorian into immediately drawing his [[weapon]]s and prompting the stormtroopers to do the same on the bounty hunter. Pershing apologized, and the Client stood to introduce the scientist before asking that Djarin lower his guns. When the bounty hunter demanded that the stormtroopers lower theirs first, stubbornly bragging about his odds to defeat the four, the Client obliged and signaled to the [[trooper]]s. With the standoff settled, Djarin sat at the Client's request and the Imperial presented a down payment of an ingot of [[beskar]], a [[metal]] used for [[Mandalorian armor]] which had been heavily plundered by the Empire during its [[Great Purge of Mandalore|purge]] of the Mandalorian [[homeworld]] of [[Mandalore]].{{BOBF|Chapter 5: Return of the Mandalorian}} The Client explained that more of the material would be handed over on delivery of "the asset" which they sought. After Pershing clarified that "the asset" that they wanted needed to be delivered alive, the Client revealed that he would also accept proof of termination for a lesser payment, a statement that did not please the scientist. When Djarin asked for the puck, the Client revealed that, for discretionary reasons, they could only provide a tracking fob, the last four digits of "the asset"'s chain code—his age of fifty [[Standard year|years]]—and the Child's last known location. The Imperial assured the Mandalorian that an individual of his skill would easily accomplish the task. Djarin took the down payment and the fob and exited the room to complete the job. As the bounty hunter did so, the Client remarked that the beskar belonged back in the Mandalorians' hands, adding that it was good to restore the natural order of things. ===The handover=== {{Quote|What are your plans for it?''"
"''How uncharacteristic of one of your reputation. You have taken both commission and payment. Is it not the code of the Guild that these events are now forgotten?|Din Djarin questions "the Client" regarding his plans for Grogu|audio=DjarinClient-Child-TMS1C3.flac|{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 3: The Sin}}}} [[File:TheClientPayment-TMCh3.png|thumb|right|300px|"The Client" offers Din Djarin the camtono of beskar in payment.]] With the data and the fob, Djarin was able to [[Mission to Arvala-7|find]] and acquire Grogu on the planet [[Arvala-7]]. He informed Karga as he made his way back to Nevarro and was advised to take "the asset" straight to the Client. When the Mandalorian arrived, the Imperial was waiting at his desk with a fob with Pershing standing at his side. Excited, the Client rose from his seat and approached the Child's [[Hover pram|hovering pram]], using the fob to confirm that he was indeed "the asset." Pershing then scanned Grogu and confirmed that he was in good health and fit for experiments. The Client then remarked that Djarin's reputation was justified, exceedingly happy that the job was complete. The bounty hunter asked him how many other hunters had fobs, to which the Imperial responded that he had to ensure the acquisition of "the asset." The Client then produced the promised payment, a [[camtono]] containing twenty ingots of beskar''[[The Mandalorian: This is the Way]]'' and handed it over to Djarin, pleased that the material was returning to a Mandalorian's care. Before he left, the Mandalorian asked what the Imperials planned to do to the infant, but the Client glared at him and refused to say, stating that per Guild tradition the transaction was complete and so should be forgotten. ===The theft=== {{Quote|I order you to extract the necessary material and be done with it.''"
"[Static] ''He has explicitly ordered us to bring it back alive.''"
"''Finish your business quickly, as I no longer can guarantee your safety.|"The Client" and Pershing, as heard on Din Djarin's long range microphone|}} After Djarin left, the Client and Pershing discussed extracting Grogu's blood. The Imperial wished for the blood to be extracted swiftly by any means possible, but the doctor kept him from harming "the asset,"''[[The Mandalorian: Allies & Enemies]]'' arguing in a confrontation later on that [[Local day|day]] that Gideon had specifically ordered Grogu to be brought back alive. In that argument, the Client told Pershing to simply extract what they needed from the Child as quickly as possible, as he could no longer promise that the doctor would be kept safe. [[File:Client-Pershing-Infrared.png|thumb|left|300px|Din Djarin spied on "the Client" and Pershing's conversation.]] Unbeknownst to the pair, Djarin was spying on their conversation. The Mandalorian had become fond of Grogu and was there to [[Incident on Nevarro|rescue]] the Child. After the Client left him, Pershing was able to retrieve some of "the asset"'s blood. At that point, Djarin broke into the safe house and liberated Grogu from Pershing, sparing the doctor. The fobs for the Child were then reactivated to entice the members of the Bounty Hunters' Guild to intercept the rogue hunter and take "the asset" back, but Djarin's [[The Tribe|Mandalorian tribe]] intervened and helped their fellow Mandalorian escape with the infant. After Djarin escaped with Grogu, the Client tightened his control over Nevarro City, with Imperial remnant reinforcements coming from an [[Nevarro Imperial base|Imperial facility]] on the far side of the planet where Pershing was experimenting with Grogu's blood. The Imperial forces [[Attack on the Tribe|attacked]] the Mandalorian tribe at its [[Nevarro Mandalorian covert|covert]] in the [[city]]'s [[Nevarro sewer|sewers]] and [[Death|killed]] many of them. The Client also used the Guild, sending its hunters out to find Djarin while he sought to lie low where the Client could not find him.''[[The Mandalorian: A Clan of Two]]'' ===The betrayals=== {{Quote|Yes, Moff Gideon?''"
"''Have they brought the child?''"
"''Yes, they have. Currently, it is sleeping.''"
"''You may wanna check again.|"The Client"'s last words, to Moff Gideon|}} With all the Guild hunters who intercepted Djarin having been killed, Karga coaxed Djarin to return to Nevarro, pretending to want help in overthrowing the Client and freeing Nevarro City from its occupation. The agent in reality intended to kill the Mandalorian and take Grogu to the Imperial. Both convened on the planet with their respective posses, but after being saved by the Child, Karga betrayed his own hunters and chose to help Djarin and his allies, the ex-[[Alliance to Restore the Republic|rebel]] [[Carasynthia Dune|Cara Dune]] and the [[Ugnaught]] [[Kuiil]], to take out the Client. [[File:Djarin-Prisoner-TMS1C7.jpg|thumb|right|300px|A cuffed Din Djarin is brought to "the Client."]] Karga and Dune escorted a [[Stuncuffs|cuffed]] Djarin to Nevarro City, intending to get close to the Client before releasing the Mandalorian and killing the Imperial. They also brought Grogu's empty pram as they made their way to the [[Nevarro school|Nevarro Common House]], which the Client used as his office. The Client himself was seated in the [[cantina]], guarded by a [[The Client's squad|squad]]{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 8: Redemption}} of stormtroopers. Rising from his seat, the Imperial inspected Djarin's new Mandalorian [[armor]], forged from the beskar that he had given to the Mandalorian. Offering to Karga a drink, he invited the agent and Djarin to sit with him at a table. The Client questioned Djarin on why Mandalore resisted Imperial rule, claiming that the Empire brought justice to every [[Star system|system]] over which it had influence. He then rhetorically asked the Mandalorian if peace had truly been restored after the Empire's fall and stated his opinion that the event had only resulted in death and chaos. The Client requested to be allowed to see Grogu with his own [[eye]]s but was informed by Karga that he was [[Sleep|asleep]]. The Imperial insisted that they would be quiet and ordered the agent to open the hovering pram before the former was interrupted by a call from Moff Gideon. [[File:Client_Shot_The_Mandalorian.png|thumb|left|300px|"The Client" was killed by Gideon's death troopers.]] The Client answered Gideon's call, with the moff asking him if Grogu was secured. The Imperial confirmed that he was in their hands and was sleeping, but Gideon told him to inspect the pram again. As the Client looked on in suspicion, a [[Gideon's guard|squad]] of Gideon's [[death trooper]]s, positioned outside the common house, immediately opened fire on the cantina, killing the Imperial, his stormtroopers, and the [[Unidentified RA-7 protocol droid bartender|protocol droid]] [[bartender]] as collateral damage.{{Topps|set=2020 Topps Star Wars Masterwork|cardname=The Client|link=https://starwarscardtrader.fandom.com/wiki/The_Client_-_Star_Wars_Masterwork_-_2020_-_Base_-_Wave_1}} Afterward, Gideon and his [[Gideon's battalion|battalion]] of troops surrounded the establishment and gave to Djarin and his allies an ultimatum to surrender Grogu. The moff's attempt was unsuccessful, as the Mandalorian and his cohort were ultimately able to [[Clash on Nevarro|escape]] the Imperial forces, killing many troopers in the process. ==Personality and traits== ===Nostalgia=== {{Quote|The Empire improves every system it touches. Judge by any metric. Safety, prosperity, trade, opportunity, peace. Compare Imperial rule to what is happening now. Look outside. Is the world more peaceful since the revolution? I see nothing but death and chaos.|"The Client," to Din Djarin|}} [[File:The_Client_and_stormtroopers.png|thumb|right|250px|"The Client" continued to serve an Imperial remnant after the Galactic Empire's fall.]] A human male standing at 1.83 [[meter]]s (6 [[foot]]), the Client had [[Color|light]] skin, white [[hair]], and light blue eyes, appearing elderly by 9 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|ABY]]. Stoic-{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 1: The Mandalorian}} {{AD|Disney+}} and stern-faced,{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 7: The Reckoning}} {{AD|Disney+}} he had a very refined, calm, and polite way of speaking. The Imperial remained calm while Din Djarin and stormtroopers drew arms in his presence and was willing to command his men to lower their weapons first. His appearance intimidated Greef Karga, who spoke cautiously when referring to him. While highly intelligent and skilled with diplomacy, the Client was not very strong nor fast, although he had a degree of skill in combat. He was not Force-sensitive. A vile and sinister person, the Client was very loyal to the Empire and looked back fondly at the [[Imperial Era|time]] when the government was in power, continuing to wear the Imperial medallion after its fall. He believed that, to every system affected by it, the late faction provided peace and prosperity and saw it as the only one worth following, claiming that only death and chaos had ensued in its absence. The Client disliked those who resisted Imperial rule and hindered what he called the "natural order of things." His expression was grave when talking about the times that had come after the Empire's end. The Client was knowledgeable in Mandalorian culture, being disheartened at the fact that their world Mandalore had resisted Imperial rule. He saw Djarin's beskar payment as a beginning to compensate for the Empire's destruction of Mandalore. As Djarin left, the Client stated that he was pleased to see the beskar returned to its rightful owners. Inspecting Djarin's newer Mandalorian armor, he complimented the craftsmanship of the traditional [[Mandalorian Armorer|Mandalorian artisans]]. The Imperial was sure to acknowledge the Mandalorian's own reputation, considering it proven when the bounty hunter brought Grogu to him. ===The asset=== {{Quote|I would like to see the baby.|"The Client," to Greef Karga|}} [[File:HeSawTheBaby.png|thumb|left|300px|"The Client" was obsessed with retrieving Grogu.]] The Client was obsessed with acquiring Grogu, being set on obtaining him by any means necessary regardless of the latter's survival. Despite having previously agreed with Pershing that they would require "the asset" to be delivered alive, he offered to Djarin the alternative of termination and claimed to be pragmatic when the scientist complained. When the Mandalorian brought Grogu to the Imperial, the Imperial rose from his seat in excitement and smiled as he inspected "the asset." The Client was both serious and secretive about his intentions with the Child, glaring at Djarin when the bounty hunter asked what would happen to the infant and in response only making an insult about how endangered the Mandalorian's kind had become. He wished for the task of acquiring Grogu's blood to be completed as soon as possible, continuing to set aside the need to keep the infant alive in the process. After Karga pretended to return "the asset" to him, he requested to be able to see the Child, insisting on opening the hovering pram despite claims that the infant was asleep. ==Equipment== {{Quote|I have a camtono of Beskar waiting for you upon the delivery of the asset.|"The Client," to Din Djarin|audio=Client-camtono.flac|}} The Client wore a black and brown fur-edged [[Clothing|coat]] over a brown shirt with dark gray trousers and black [[boot]]s. His Imperial medallion was hung around his neck. He also possessed a camtono of beskar that had been taken during the Great Purge of Mandalore. ==Behind the scenes== ===Portrayal milestones=== {{Quote|My part makes the basic ingredients of the story.|Werner Herzog, on his role as "the Client"|{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/mandalorian-why-werner-herzog-called-jon-favreau-a-coward-1254941|text=The 'Mandalorian' Moment That Caused Werner Herzog to Call His Bosses "Cowards"|author=Aaron Couch|date=2019-11-15|quote=Producers Jon Favreau and Dave Filoni drew laughs at a 'Star Wars' event when recalling the actor's reaction to a particular choice on set.|archivedate=20220429204922}}}} [[File:Client-concept.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Concept art for "the Client" by Brian Matyas.]] "The Client" first appeared in "[[Chapter 1: The Mandalorian]]," the debut episode of the [[Disney+]] television show ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]''{{'s}} [[The Mandalorian Season One|first season]], which was directed by [[Dave Filoni]] and aired on [[November 12]], [[2019]]. The character also appeared in "[[Chapter 3: The Sin]]" and "[[Chapter 7: The Reckoning]]," later episodes of the season that were directed by [[Deborah Chow]] and released on [[November 22]] and [[December 18]] of that year.{{InsiderCite|201|Star Wars: The Mandalorian Season One Companion|''Star Wars: The Mandalorian'' Season One Companion}} The Client was portrayed by the award-winning film director [[Werner Herzog]], with [[John Dixon]] serving as a stunt double for him in "Chapter 7: The Reckoning." While Herzog was included in ''The Mandalorian''{{'s}} initial casting announcement on [[December 12]], [[2018]],{{SW|url=news/pedro-pascal-revealed-as-the-mandalorian|text=Pedro Pascal Revealed as ''The Mandalorian''}} the character of the Client was first mentioned in the show's panel at [[Celebration Chicago]] on [[April 14]], 2019.{{SW|url=news/swcc-2019-9-things-we-learned-from-the-mandalorian-panel|text=SWCC 2019: 9 Things We Learned from ''The Mandalorian'' Panel}} The character then appeared in the show's official trailer, published on [[Wikipedia:YouTube|YouTube]] on [[August 24]] of that year.{{SWYouTube|aOC8E8z_ifw|The Mandalorian | Official Trailer | Disney+ | Streaming Nov. 12|sw_url=video/the-mandalorian-official-trailer}} His credited title of "the Client" was first mentioned on [[the Walt Disney Company]]'s Direct-to-Consumer & International website on [[December 27]].{{Disney|subdomain=dmedmedia|url=disney-plus/the-mandalorian/photos|text=Episodic Photos}} According to [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] member [[Pablo Hidalgo]], the writers for ''The Mandalorian'' explicitly did not want "the Client" to be given a name.{{Twitter|pabl0hidalgo|status/1725309173603414308|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|date=2023-11-16|quote=and if production doesn't want them named, they don't get named. Looking at you, the Client.|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/auhbZ}} ===Recruitment and conception=== {{Quote|I was just thinking Italian mob boss for the Client. I was shocked that they got Werner Herzog, because he's such an iconic actor and director.|Brian Matyas, on visually designing "the Client"|[[The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian (Season One)|''The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian'' Season One]]}} [[File:Herzog-Mando-Makers.png|thumb|left|300px|Werner Herzog in the safe house set with showrunner Jon Favreau (center) and director and producer Dave Filoni (left)]] Herzog was invited to play ''The Mandalorian'' by its showrunner and creator, [[Jon Favreau]],{{YouTube|video=wreLS1luB8I|text=Werner Herzog praises new 'Star Wars' series 'Mandalorian'|channel=@ap|name=Associated Press|date=2019-05-04|quote=Werner Herzog is calling "The Mandalorian" "a phenomenal achievement" after joining the cast of the streaming series set in the "Star Wars" universe.}} who was reportedly very set on having him for the role.{{StarWarsShow|WTNw6ASa3VE|Anthony Daniels Graces Us With His Presence and We Attend The Mandalorian Fan Event|sw_url=video/anthony-daniels-graces-us-with-his-presence-and-we-attend-the-mandalorian-fan-event|date=2019-11-20}} The highly acclaimed director's only knowledge of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' saga by that point had been from trailers and excerpts as, by his own account, he did not watch many films. He likewise had no knowledge of Favreau's past work but believed that the showrunner admired his acting,{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2019/tv/news/werner-herzog-the-mandalorian-star-wars-jon-favreau-disney-plus-1203400810|text=Werner Herzog on Why He Didn't Need to See 'Star Wars' Films for 'The Mandalorian' Role|author=[https://variety.com/author/will-thorne Thorne, Will]|date=2019-11-12|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|quote=At first sight, playing a vital character in Jon Favreau's "The Mandalorian," Disney's live-action "Star Wars" series, which the studio is using to launch its ambitious streaming venture, might appear to be an odd move for Werner Herzog.|archivedate=20220806191139}} and requested to look at the screenplay. The filmmaker liked what he saw of the screenplay given to him{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/werner-herzog-interview-family-romance-llc-the-mandalorian|text=Werner Herzog on 'Family Romance, LLC', Shooting in Japan, and Why He Joined 'The Mandalorian'|author=[https://collider.com/author/helen-barlow Barlow, Helen]|date=2019-06-03|work=[[Wikipedia:Collider (website)|Collider]]|quote=The filmmaker discusses his new film at the Cannes Film Festival.|archivedate=20200809005449}} and felt that the dark, untrustworthy figure pitched to him would be easy to play.{{YouTube|video=O6qAf9Q33qg|text=THE MANDALORIAN cast Q&A|channel=@FabTVcom|name=FabTV|date=2019-11-14|quote=THE MANDALORIAN cast , director, producer, Q&A with Gina Carano.}} Herzog also saw the acting job as an opportunity to earn money back after financing his 2019 film [[Wikipedia:Family Romance, LLC|''Family Romance, LLC'']] with his own means. Artist [[Brian Matyas]] created concept art of the Client after Herzog was cast to play the character. The artist based the character's design on depictions of Italian [[Wikipedia:Mafia|mafia]] bosses. Filming for "Chapter 1: The Mandalorian" and "Chapter 3: The Sin" took place between [[October 1]] and [[October 26]] in 2018, while "Chapter 7: The Reckoning" was filmed shortly thereafter, from [[October 29]] to [[November]] 12. Due to reasons of secrecy, during production of ''The Mandalorian'' Herzog was led to believe that the series had a completely different title.{{YouTube|video=af12yiPAdK4|text=Werner Herzog Q&A: The Mandalorian|channel=@VivaVideography|name=VivaVideography|date=2019-11-23|quote=Legendary director and occasional actor Werner Herzog talks with IndieWire's Anne Thompson about his role as "The Client" in Jon Favreau's new Disney+ Star Wars series "The Mandalorian."}} The actor was also contracted for a [[Wikipedia:Huckleberry Finn|Huckleberry Finn]] movie as a false trail. The secrecy policies went as far as to prohibit Werner and other actors from leaving the studio during the shoot, even for lunch, unless they concealed their costume completely, with a security guard checking people out at the gate. Herzog was aware of fans getting into the lot to try and capture photos of the shoots.{{BookCite|author=Herzog, Werner|title=Every Man for Himself and God against All: A Memoir|publisher=[[Wikipedia:Random House|Random House]]|date=[[2023]]|isbn=9781529193701}} ===Production and characterization=== {{Quote|I can say that filmmaking—and that's Jon's great achievement with "The Mandalorian"—is brought back to where it always has been. As an actor, you see where you are, the planet on which you're moving, and the camera could even be on the shoulder of a cinematographer and move around, and that's how filmmaking has been and should be. As an actor, I knew it immediately this was good stuff. You feel it when the camera doesn't have to be motion-controlled and you don't have to act like a robot.|Werner Herzog, on the production of ''The Mandalorian''|}} [[File:Chow-Herzog-S1Guide.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Werner Herzog with director Deborah Chow on the set of "Chapter 7: The Reckoning"]] With the ''Star Wars'' universe being new to him, Herzog was briefed on his character and the setting, coming to question whether the stormtroopers were the Client's allies or enemies. He was deeply fascinated by the technology of ''The Mandalorian''{{'s}} set, [[Wikipedia:StageCraft|The Volume]], calling it a step out of the "obsolete" use of green screens as one could better view the environment in which their character performed during the filming process.{{YouTube|video=S5GIaEPvyYE|text=Werner Herzog Talks THE MANDALORIAN, Baby Yoda and Being A Documentary Filmmaker|channel=@jakethemovieguy|name=Jake's Takes|date=2020-08-26|quote=Emmy-Winner Jake Hamilton talks with documentary filmmaker Werner Herzog about THE MANDALORIAN, Baby Yoda and Being a Documentary Filmmaker}} For one scene of "Chapter 1: The Mandalorian" involving Greef Karga and Din Djarin in the Nevarro Common House, Karga's actor [[Carl Weathers]] attempted to convey the Client's power over Karga by trying to sound more cautious when discussing Herzog's character than he was when generally talking to the Mandalorian. Weathers highly respected Herzog and his work, referring to the acclaimed filmmaker as "maestro" throughout the entire time during which the pair worked together on set.{{Spotify|url=episode/6d1II4UU5BvMmOCffRtdIg?si=869epKwvSe6QNtc7FhUClw|text=Still Watching: The Mandalorian—"Chapter One" with Jon Favreau and Carl Weathers|quote=Joanna Robinson and Anthony Breznican of Vanity Fair return to a galaxy far far away for "Chapter One" the series premiere of The Mandalorian on Disney+.}} In a later interview, the actor reflected that working with Herzog was the highlight of his career.{{InsiderCite|194|Carl Weathers: The Weathers Report}} ===Further collaboration=== {{Quote|I was so happy to be on a Star Wars set, and I let a little of it show in front of Werner. I said, 'Isn't this exciting?' and he looked at me and replied, 'This is serious work. We are creating characters that would not otherwise exist! We are breathing life into them.'|Christ Bartlett recalls speaking with Werner Herzog on set|{{InsiderCite|215|He Is the Droid You're Looking For!}}}} [[File:Client-troopers-BTS.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The Client on the set of "Chapter 7: The Reckoning" with some actors playing stormtroopers.]] At one point, Herzog watched the filming of a scene with [[Chris Bartlett]], the body double for a number of characters in ''The Mandalorian'', including the protocol droid bartender that fell with the Client, on one of the latter's first days on set. Bartlett recalled being unable to completely contain his excitement about being on a ''Star Wars'' set, asking Herzog, whom he believed to be a great actor, if he also found it exciting. According to Bartlett, Herzog responded that they were doing serious work by creating characters that otherwise would not exist and breathing life into them, which Bartlett reflected to [[Star Wars Insider|''Star Wars'' Insider]] was totally true. In that interview with ''Insider'' contributor [[Pat Jankiewicz]], he recalled Herzog's words as an amazing thirty-second long acting masterclass. Filoni later remarked that the Client was one of the first human faces that he ever filmed in live-action;{{DisneyGallery|Connections}} the director's experience up to that point had been confined to animation projects such as ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''.{{DisneyGallery|Directing}} Herzog considered his part in ''The Mandalorian''{{'s}} first season as providing the "basic ingredients" of the story. After understanding more about the ''Star Wars'' universe, he considered it to be similar in nature to an expanding mythology and a new way of seeing peoples' roles in the universe.{{WebCite|url=https://www.empireonline.com/movies/news/werner-herzog-not-dismiss-star-wars-new-mythologies|text=Werner Herzog Says We 'Should Not Dismiss' Star Wars: 'They Are New Mythologies'|author=Sophie Butcher|date=2023-10-24|work=[[Wikipedia:Empire (magazine)|''Empire'']]|quote=We should not dismiss ''Star Wars'': they are new mythologies and a new way of seeing our role in the universe.|archivedate=20231102162419}} In his memoires, Herzog said that a downside of his role in a ''Star Wars'' production was that it took attention away from his own books and films. ===Werner would like to see the baby=== {{Quote|Filmmaking now, all of a sudden, is back to almost "old school." Technology becomes invisible and that's a great thing. Yoda baby, beautiful, and it moves in there, too. The guys who are moving the eyes and the lips and the facial expressions, phenomenal. And they filmed it one-on-one. It was heartbreakingly beautiful.|Werner Herzog, on Grogu|{{DisneyGallery|Practical}}}} [[File:Pershing-Client_on_set.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Werner Herzog and Omid Abtahi, Doctor Pershing's actor, on set with Grogu's puppet]] Upon first seeing Grogu, known to many as "Baby Yoda," Herzog was astounded by how realistically the puppet and the animatronic for the character worked and saw it as a great mechanical achievement, calling it "heartbreakingly beautiful." According to Chow, when she was shooting the Client and Grogu's scene in "Chapter 3: The Sin," Herzog was so entranced with the Child's puppet that he seemingly forgot that the baby was a puppet at all, starting to direct it as if it were a person. At the end of that shot, Chow and [[Jason Porter]], a visual effects supervisor for [[Industrial Light & Magic]] (ILM), performed a "plate shot," where the puppet was removed and ILM could implement a [[Wikipedia:Computer-generated imagery|CGI]] version of Grogu in case the practical shot was not satisfactory. Herzog disliked the decision, considering the Child's practical look to be a great step forward for filming. He reportedly told the creators to commit to the magic of the puppet and called them all cowards. Favreau and Filoni, who were among the recipients of Herzog's complaint, came to agree and used Grogu's puppet for the shots as much as possible, making sure that the CGI—the rendered Baby Yoda—did not exceed the puppet's abilities. ===Adaptation differences=== {{Quote|I am simply being practical. Bounty hunting is an uncertain business.|An alternate line by "the Client" from ''Star Wars: The Mandalorian Junior Novel''|}} [[Joe Schreiber]]'s [[2021]] [[The Mandalorian Junior Novel|junior novelization]] of ''The Mandalorian''{{'s}} first season presents a number of the Client's lines differently to how they were said or presented in the show. The [[2020]] storybook ''[[The Mandalorian: A Clan of Two]]'', written by [[Brooke Vitale]], states that the Client's [[soldier]]s attacked Din Djarin's group, injuring Greef Karga, whereas in Chapter 7, the attackers were a flock of [[Nevarro reptavian]]s.
